checks.measured: HEAD == baseline fe923fe21d2c9116940c7f83f22ef274ebe818c1. The 11 tracked baseline changes plus the single untracked candidate file (terminal-repair.md), less the generated review record, the T038 package record, and the eight regenerated phase8-T038 stage records, form the exact 12-path candidate union recorded in reviewed_paths and in reports/xcom-queue/t038-package.json after regeneration. git diff --check is clean. No file in the union is a generated stage/package/review artifact (J-077 satisfied).

checks.name: R1 required gRPC transport and generated-client surface
checks.command_or_evidence: independent inspection of the admitted offline prefix and package envelope: ldd on the admitted libgrpc++.so.1.30.2 / libgrpc.so.10.0.0 / libgrpc++_unsecure / libgrpc_unsecure, nm over the admitted static libgrpc.a and libgrpc_unsecure.a, search for any c-ares runtime/header, and comparison against the pinned package manifest digest
checks.measured: R1 is NOT closed and is not falsely claimed. The admitted shared gRPC runtimes all carry NEEDED libcares.so.2 and the loader reports it unresolved; no libcares runtime or ares.h exists in the admitted prefix, in the admitted package manifest, or on the host; the admitted static libraries retain 15 undefined ares_* symbols each, so static linking cannot satisfy them either. The candidate therefore keeps the accepted T031/T032 custom length/method framing as an explicitly unclaimed floor and does not substitute it for the contracted gRPC service. Closing R1 requires admitting the complete pinned gRPC runtime (at minimum a c-ares runtime) into the offline envelope, which is a host-side dependency change outside this repair; it is carried to external acceptance as an unresolved P1 blocker.

checks.name: R2 declared wire-field validation and zero rejected-side effects
checks.command_or_evidence: independent compilation and execution of the authoritative host probe automation/reviews/t030-t038-20260929/gateway_probes.cpp against the assembled library set, plus source inspection of GatewaySession::SubmitStimulation and the added XcomToolGatewayNegative cases
checks.measured: SubmitStimulation validates interaction, direction, schedule mode, clock domain, and contract identity before any emission or enqueue; the declared interaction is preserved through the accepted guard/action path instead of being rewritten from the action. All four external negative probes (mismatched interaction, mismatched direction, unknown schedule enum 99, unmapped clock) and the valid control pass: rejected requests produce one rejected outcome with emitter call count zero. The candidate regression cases confirm zero emission and zero pending retention on each rejection, and a contract mismatch is rejected rather than dropped.

checks.name: R3 bounded scheduled queue and eventual execution
checks.command_or_evidence: external probes RejectUnauthorizedScheduledTarget and PendingQueueRemainsBoundedAcrossTicks, source inspection of SubmitStimulation and StimulationActionPath::execute/queue/drain, and the added XcomToolGatewayBounds scheduled cases
checks.measured: Scheduled work is no longer a bare counter: capacity is checked against the accepted action-path queue depth before enqueue, the request and payload are retained in the accepted StimulationActionPath bounded queue, and on_idle_tick drains due work through the accepted scheduler into real emitted/expired terminal outcomes. The external bound probe holds pending at or below the configured maximum across re-submission and flow-credit replenishment, and the candidate regressions confirm eventual execution when due, expiry past the late window, and no retention for an unauthorized/clock-unmapped scheduled target.

checks.name: R4 per-request deadlines anchored to request arrival
checks.command_or_evidence: external probe EachRequestReceivesItsOwnDeadline, source inspection of GatewaySession::admit and on_idle_tick, and the added XcomToolGatewayBounds/Lifecycle deadline and idle cases
checks.measured: Admission now anchors the request deadline to the request's own declared arrival tick in the bound domain rather than to the fixed session-creation tick, so a session created at tick 0 accepts a fresh valid request at tick 500 with a 100-unit deadline (the external probe emits as before). Idle timeout is likewise measured from the last admitted activity, not from session creation.

checks.name: R5 observation-stream ownership
checks.command_or_evidence: external probe FirstStreamSurvivesSecondOpen, source inspection of OpenObservation/ReadObservations/CloseObservation/detach_all_streams_locked, and the added XcomToolGatewayLifecycle.IndependentObservationStreamsClose case
checks.measured: Each accepted stream now owns an independent bounded handle in a per-session list capped by max_streams_per_session; opening a second stream no longer overwrites the first, and the external probe confirms the first stream handle still closes cleanly after a second open. Read, close, and disconnect address the exact requested stream identity and the active counter tracks the retained handles.

checks.name: R6 exact lease-release identity
checks.command_or_evidence: external probe ReleaseRequiresExactLeaseIdentity, source inspection of GatewaySession::ReleaseLease, and the added XcomToolGatewayLifecycle.LeaseReleaseRequiresExactIdentity case plus the synthetic separate-process client lease test
checks.measured: ReleaseLease compares the supplied lease identity against the exact held lease identity and rejects a mismatched or stale identity without releasing or mutating lease/session state; the external probe confirms a wrong identity never returns a released state, while the synthetic client that sends the acquired identity still releases successfully.

checks.command_or_evidence: ctest --test-dir build/f8u (full unit measure) and python3 engineering/check_xcom_traceability.py --verify reports/xcom-queue/t038-traceability.json
checks.measured: 510 of 510 CTest cases pass in the assembled subtree (the 496 baseline cases plus the 14 added T031 regression cases), including all 84 gateway and synthetic-client cases. The traceability verifier passes with candidate_revision_state working-tree and, in the disposable committed clone, committed; the material digest is identical in both states. observations: R1 (P1, transport) is the only finding not closed by this repair, and it is not closed by a substitute. It is independently reproduced as an external admitted-envelope blocker, not a candidate code defect: the admitted gRPC shared libraries require an absent c-ares runtime and the admitted static libraries keep undefined c-ares symbols, with no ares runtime or header in the admitted prefix, the admitted package manifest, or the host. The candidate keeps the accepted T031/T032 custom framing only as an explicitly unclaimed floor and never presents it as the contracted gRPC service. An intentional contract change would need an explicit scope decision; admitting the complete pinned gRPC runtime is a host-side offline dependency change outside this repair. External acceptance must disposition this P1 item.

The remaining eight findings (R2-R9) are independently verified closed by the authoritative external probes, by targeted source inspection, and by independent full-command negative probes that mutate and restore real retained files. No repaired behaviour relies only on the repair agent's claims or on a green suite.

R4 residual note: because admission now anchors the deadline to the request's own arrival, the literal 'now greater than now plus deadline' comparison in admit() is structurally unreachable, so a freshly arrived request is never expired at admission; the meaningful remaining bound is the accepted action-path guard and permit validity (an out-of-permit request is still rejected with zero emission), and the declared schedule must fall inside the request deadline window. This is a benign dead-comparison comment-level residual, not an observable behaviour defect.

R3 residual note: the gateway enforces its own max_pending_requests ceiling before enqueue while the accepted action path also enforces its own max_pending_actions; both are finite bounds, and the lower effective ceiling is the gateway value. This is consistent with the accepted scheduler and is recorded for completeness.

R7 bound scope: both the benchmark verifier and the traceability verifier were exercised in the working-tree state and in a disposable clone committed as the direct child of the baseline; no commit or ref was created in the candidate repository.

Inherited condition (not one of R1-R9): running engineering/run_phase6_conformance.py directly at accumulated HEAD fails because T037 changed Doxyfile relative to the pinned Phase 6 baseline. This is an accepted-baseline condition carried under the T035 evidence; the Phase 8 trusted wrapper isolates the Phase 6 checker at the pinned revision and passes.
limitations: This is a read-only internal review of the uncommitted T030-T038 repair candidate; the review record is the only artifact written and no production code or test was edited.

R1 remains an unresolved external P1 blocker; this review neither accepts it nor changes the accepted tool-gateway contract, and it does not establish external acceptance, terminal re-review, or platform-main delivery.

The full isolated-platform build was not re-created; the assembled build/f8u tree was reused for the unit measure and the independently compiled external probes, so the cross-process integration evidence is the retained trusted record rather than a fresh rerun in this review.
The committed-candidate verifier branches were exercised in a disposable clone; the candidate repository, its index, and its refs were left unchanged.
No production performance, timing, transport, compatibility, or live-readiness claim is made.
method: Read-only inspection of the exact 12-path candidate union and its baseline diff; independent compilation and execution of the authoritative host gateway probe against the assembled library set; independent full-command negative probes that delete predecessor requirement records, remove predecessor verification edges, and inject synthetic absolute host paths into retained package and record files, each with byte-exact restore and post-restore re-verification; independent reproduction of the gRPC runtime blocker via loader and symbol inspection; execution of the repository-owned benchmark and traceability verifiers in the working-tree state and in a disposable clone committed as the direct child of the baseline; the trusted Phase 8 conformance wrapper in the committed clone; the full 510-case assembled unit suite; and a public-safety scan of every retained file this review writes.
